paper_title: Low-Energy Supernovae Severely Constrain Radiative Particle Decays
coupling_convention: G_agamma in GeV^-1, as plotted on y-axis of Fig. 2
notes: Paper (Caputo, Janka, Raffelt, Vitagliano, arXiv:2201.09890) presents a new astrophysical bound on ALP-photon coupling from low-energy supernovae, requiring radiative decay energy deposition in the progenitor mantle < 0.1 B. Coupling type is unambiguous (G_agamma, a->2gamma). No numerical table is provided; the exclusion region is shown in Fig. 2 (red-shaded, R*=5e13 cm, 0.1 B). Data points are an approximate reconstruction of the LOWER boundary of the excluded band based on the abstract (couplings 1e-10 to 1e-8 GeV^-1 excluded for 1-500 MeV masses) and the stated scaling G ∝ 1/m_a at low masses with coalescence-driven minimum near m_a ~ 100-200 MeV and Boltzmann-suppression rise toward 500 MeV. The excluded region is a closed band (upper boundary at λ≈R_NS not extracted). Not a dark-matter search, so no local DM density assumed.
